summary: Stage 2 preserves the strong measured chassis and complete 73-key presentation, adds all four required input paths, deterministic lifecycle/sustain/polyphony/velocity coverage, useful status feedback, and a cleanly separated piano engine, input layer, and Web Audio backend. The implementation is nevertheless only a partial piano recreation: its six root AudioBuffers are generated at startup from a four-partial additive waveform rather than recorded or comparably convincing piano samples; piano type/model, Timbre, and Dynamic Compression largely change names or display state without changing the audio; the Web Audio graph itself has no focused tests; and the no-Web-Audio fallback is silent while the UI calls it ready. All 25 tests and the test/typecheck/lint/build gates pass. Saved 1440x900 and 390x844 renders support the visual ratings, but this evaluator could not repeat live browser or audible verification because no in-app browser target was available.

criteria.label: Reference fidelity retention
evidence: Direct comparison of evidence/stage2-desktop.png with prompts/NS4_HA73_TopDown-01_241008.jpg shows that the Stage 1 connected red chassis, six inset sections, slate/red palette, full keybed, material hierarchy, and low 3.095:1 silhouette remain intact after the piano/status additions.

The Stage 1 assessment and the direct reference comparison identify the retained limitation: the panel remains a schematic approximation with oversized/invented OLED regions, simplified physical control placement, and tiny legends; Stage 2 does not visibly regress it, but cannot merit exceptional reference fidelity.

criteria.label: Responsive chassis
evidence: evidence/stage2-visual-audit.md records a 1353.6 x 437.3 px desktop chassis at 94% viewport width, the required 3.095 aspect ratio and 54/46 deck-keybed split, and a 374.4 x 121 px narrow chassis with document width 390; the saved files are the required 1440x900 and 390x844 dimensions.

evidence/stage2-narrow.png visibly keeps both end cheeks and all 73 keys inside one chassis without horizontal clipping or a white gutter. The whole-surface scaling makes panel labels and individual keys extremely small, so narrow usability is strong structurally but not exceptional.

criteria.label: Input coverage
evidence: src/components/Keyboard.tsx uses pointer events and per-key pointer capture for mouse, pen, and touch; src/piano/InputController.ts maps 18 computer keys with repeat suppression and release-all; src/piano/MidiInput.ts parses note on/off, velocity-zero note-off, and CC64 across MIDI channels and reports unsupported, disconnected, permission-denied, and error states.

The passing Keyboard, InputController, MidiInput, and App tests exercise pointer/touch velocity, mapped key press/release, repeat suppression, cleanup, MIDI routing/velocity/sustain, no-input, and denied-permission paths. Concurrent multi-touch and physical MIDI were not directly exercised.

criteria.label: Piano controls
evidence: src/App.tsx lines 84-90 wire Piano enable, Master Level, Piano A level, Reverb on/off, and Reverb mix into the engine, while the status Sustain button and MIDI CC64 drive sustain. The engine tests confirm clamped volume/reverb values reach the injected audio boundary.

Manual pages 23-26 specify piano type/model, KB Touch, Dynamic Compression, Timbre, acoustics, sustain, and layer behavior. In src/App.tsx lines 123-139, type/model, Timbre, and Dynamic Compression only alter React selection/display text and never alter the audio backend; Unison, Pedal Noise, String Resonance, Soft Release, KB Touch, Piano B level, and manual half-pedaling behavior are not implemented.

criteria.label: Display and status feedback
evidence: src/App.tsx lines 129-131 contextually update Piano, Program, and Effects displays with type/model, timbre/dynamic setting, voice count, sample mode, sustain, and reverb state; lines 184-189 expose model, voice count, audio readiness, sustain, MIDI state, and Panic in the status row.

The passing App test directly verifies computer-key pressed state, voice-count status, Sustain, and Panic feedback. MIDI denial/unsupported states are represented by the button label, but error detail is discarded and the status does not identify active note names or distinguish a silent no-Web-Audio fallback from playable audio.

criteria.label: Piano sound source
evidence: src/piano/WebAudioBackend.ts lines 6-25 creates only six 3.2-second mono root buffers at runtime from a fundamental plus three sine partials, then pitch-shifts the nearest root. This is oscillator-derived buffer playback, not the manual's multi-velocity, carefully sampled piano library or a comparably convincing modeled source.

The Stage 2 tests fake PianoAudioBackend and do not instantiate or audition WebAudioPianoBackend, so there is no exercised evidence that the generated bank is musically convincing. The implementation exceeds a single live oscillator architecturally but remains a substantially incorrect substitute for the required sampled piano.

criteria.label: Note lifecycle
evidence: The passing PianoEngine tests exercise note-on/off, same-note retrigger with release of the old handle, all-notes-off, immediate stop, and distinct-note polyphony; App/InputController tests exercise key-up and focus-loss cleanup paths.

src/piano/WebAudioBackend.ts lines 84-117 applies an 8 ms attack, scheduled release, and stop handling. Same-pitch inputs are stored by MIDI number and replace one another rather than supporting overlapping ownership, and the actual Web Audio envelope/ended cleanup is not covered by a backend test, limiting the rating below exceptional.

criteria.label: Velocity response
evidence: The passing tests exercise the clamped nonlinear velocityToGain curve at negative, zero, low, mid, maximum, and over-range values and verify touch pointer depth forwards velocity 120; MIDI tests verify incoming velocity 120 reaches the target.

src/components/Keyboard.tsx maps pointer depth to velocity 55-127, computer keys use a fixed 104, and MIDI preserves input velocity. The manual's KB Touch modes and Dynamic Compression behavior do not affect the curve, and there are no recorded multi-velocity sample layers.

criteria.label: Sustain and polyphony
evidence: The passing PianoEngine tests exercise held-to-sustained transitions, pedal-up release, Panic, a deterministic oldest-voice steal at the configured limit, and cleanup; the production engine defaults to 32 voices and MIDI tests exercise CC64 down/up parsing.

The implementation provides useful boolean sustain and polyphony, but the manual page 26 half-pedaling, sostenuto/soft-pedal behavior, pedal-down samples, and pedal-noise dynamics are absent. WebAudioPianoBackend voice disposal and 32-voice load are not directly exercised.

criteria.label: Playability
evidence: Source and passing tests support reliable mapped-key triggering, repeat suppression, pointer capture, velocity forwarding, MIDI routing, sustain, blur cleanup, and a 32-voice engine; WebAudioPianoBackend requests latencyHint 'interactive' and resumes on note-on.

No live or audible pass was available to this evaluator, multi-touch concurrency is not tested, the computer map spans only 18 notes, and the oscillator-derived 3.2-second samples plus same-pitch ownership limitation are important sustained-play gaps.

criteria.label: Control feedback
evidence: The passing App and Keyboard tests show immediate pressed-key, voice-count, Sustain, and Panic feedback; source inspection shows Master/Piano level and Reverb controls update the engine while OLED content updates for model, timbre, dynamic setting, voices, sustain, and effect state.

There is no end-to-end UI test proving panel parameter changes reach the audio graph, meters remain fixed at 72, and model/type/Timbre/Dynamic controls give visual feedback without corresponding audible changes, making feedback only partially coherent.

criteria.label: Failure handling
evidence: Passing tests cover MIDI with no inputs, permission denial, mapped-key release-all, Panic, and a backend-reported sample fallback; source also handles pointer cancellation/lost capture and window blur.

createBrowserPianoBackend returns SilentPianoBackend when Web Audio is unavailable, yet App labels fallback mode 'offline piano ready'; AudioContext construction/resume failures are not caught, the sample-loader failure path is not used by the app, and MIDI error detail is discarded from the UI.

criteria.label: Audio architecture
evidence: PianoEngine.ts defines an injectable audio boundary and owns deterministic state/voice policy; WebAudioBackend.ts owns nodes/samples; InputController.ts and MidiInput.ts isolate input parsing; App.tsx binds UI state to those layers. This separation makes the fake-backed deterministic suite clear and maintainable.

The architecture is weakened by audio-significant piano parameters living only in App display state, no modeled program/piano-patch object, and no focused WebAudioBackend tests for graph topology, parameter automation, sample selection, or cleanup.

criteria.label: Performance and cleanup
evidence: Independent reruns pass all 7 files/25 tests, typecheck, ESLint with zero warnings, and the production build; source cleans window listeners, MIDI handlers, pointer captures, held notes, voices on Panic/unmount, and backend voice entries on source end.

The AudioContext and permanent master/dry/wet/convolver graph are never closed or disconnected, the six sample buffers and impulse are generated synchronously during initial render, naturally ended sources can remain represented in PianoEngine until note-off, and backend cleanup/performance under rapid 32-voice play is untested. No live console pass could be repeated in this evaluator session.

issues: The piano sound source is a six-root additive waveform bank rendered into AudioBuffers at startup, not credible recorded multi-velocity piano samples or comparably convincing modeling.
Piano type/model, Timbre, and Dynamic Compression update selection/display state but do not change the generated sound; several manual Piano controls are decorative or absent.
The Web Audio backend has no direct tests for attack/release automation, dry/wet routing, source cleanup, sample selection, or load behavior; most audio tests stop at a fake boundary.
The no-Web-Audio fallback is silent while the UI reports 'offline piano ready', and AudioContext construction/resume errors are not surfaced.
Narrow rendering avoids clipping but makes the full panel and keys too small for practical touch use.

Live browser and audible verification could not be repeated because the in-app browser exposed no target; ratings use fresh saved evidence, the verification record, direct source/manual comparison, and independently rerun deterministic checks.
